_comment: Hand-written background stories for games history.dat does not describe (mostly TeknoParrot / PC-based arcade games). Key = the item name the game lists use (case-insensitive). New-GameStories.py prefers these over every other source. Keep it to facts a player would recognise; no records, sales figures or dates you are not sure of. ASCII only.

AAA.title: America's Army Arcade
AAA.story: An arcade shooter built on America's Army, the free PC game the U.S. Army used to show what soldier training looks like. Players hold mounted rifles and work through training ranges and missions, scored on accuracy and on following the rules of engagement, not just on how much they hit.
special: Based on a game the U.S. Army itself made and gave away for free on PC.
Rewards careful, accurate shooting over spraying bullets.

Batman.title: Batman
Batman.story: A sit-down racing game in which you drive Batmobiles through Gotham City, chasing the Joker, Penguin and other villains. The garage spans the car's history, from the 1960s TV show to the armoured Tumbler of the Dark Knight films, each with its own handling and weapons.
special: Batmobiles from several eras of the TV series and films in one game.
Combines street racing with boss chases against Batman's villains.

BBCF.title: BlazBlue: Central Fiction
BBCF.story: The last chapter of the BlazBlue story, Arc System Works' 2D fighting series known for its hand-drawn, high-resolution sprites and dense lore. Every character has a unique Drive mechanic, which gives the large cast very different ways to play.
special: Brings the BlazBlue story arc to its conclusion.
Each fighter's Drive button works differently: no two characters play alike.

BorderBreakScramble.title: Border Break Scramble
BorderBreakScramble.story: Sega's online robot battle game: teams of players pilot customisable mechs called Blasts and fight over each other's cores in large team matches across Japan's arcades. The cabinet uses a joystick-style controller plus a mouse to aim, like a PC shooter.
special: Team battles between arcades across Japan, played online.
Mouse aiming in an arcade cabinet.

DariusBurst.title: Dariusburst: Another Chronicle
DariusBurst.story: A Darius horizontal shooter on an extra-wide cabinet: two screens side by side make one long playfield, and up to four players fly together against Taito's giant robotic sea creatures. The branching zone map and the warning screen before each huge boss are series trademarks.
special: Two screens joined into one ultra-wide playfield, like the original 1986 Darius cabinet.
Up to four players at once.
Bosses are giant mechanical fish, a Darius tradition.

EADP.title: Elevator Action Death Parade
EADP.story: A light-gun game that turns Taito's 1983 spy classic Elevator Action into a two-player shooting gallery. Agents ride elevators floor by floor through an enemy building, ducking and firing as the doors open.
special: A gun-game sequel to the 1983 Elevator Action.
The action is staged around elevator doors opening on each floor.

FNF.title: The Fast and the Furious
FNF.story: Raw Thrills' street racer based on the film series: tuned import cars, nitrous boosts and races through city streets. It helped re-establish the sit-down driving cabinet in American arcades and started a run of Fast and Furious arcade games.
special: Licensed from the Fast and the Furious films.
Followed by Super Bikes, Drift and SuperCars games in the same series.

GGXrd.title: Guilty Gear Xrd REV2
GGXrd.story: A 2D fighting game that is actually made of 3D models, drawn and animated so carefully that it looks hand-drawn. Arc System Works limited the animation frames and hand-tuned every pose so the characters move like anime sprites. REV2 is the final arcade update of Xrd.
special: 3D models made to look exactly like 2D animation.
Its art technique influenced later anime-style fighting games.

GGXX.title: Guilty Gear XX Accent Core Plus R
GGXX.story: The last revision of Guilty Gear XX, Arc System Works' fast 2D fighting game with a heavy-metal soundtrack. Plus R rebalanced the whole cast after years of play on the earlier versions.
special: The final version of the Guilty Gear XX line.
Known for its rock and metal soundtrack and very fast, technical play.

GHA.title: Guitar Hero Arcade
GHA.story: The arcade version of Activision's Guitar Hero: play along to rock songs on a guitar-shaped controller, hitting the coloured fret buttons and the strum bar in time with the notes. Tilting the guitar up triggers Star Power.
special: Brought the home rhythm-game hit into arcades.
Tilt the guitar up for Star Power, as on the home version.

GRID.title: GRID
GRID.story: An arcade version of Codemasters' Race Driver: GRID, the circuit racer known for its damage modelling and racing cars from touring cars to supercars. Released in arcades through Sega with linked cabinets for multiplayer.
special: Based on the PC and console racer Race Driver: GRID.
Linked cabinets let players race each other.

HOTD4SP.title: The House of the Dead 4 Special
HOTD4SP.story: A larger attraction version of The House of the Dead 4. Two players sit in an enclosed booth with a big screen and a seat that moves with the action, picking up the story right after House of the Dead 4.
special: A theatre-style cabinet with a moving seat.
Continues the story of The House of the Dead 4.

ID6.title: Initial D Arcade Stage 6 AA
ID6.story: Mountain-pass street racing from the Initial D manga and anime: race on Japanese touge roads, drifting through hairpins in Japanese cars. A card saves your car, tune-ups and progress, so players kept coming back to the same cabinet for years.
special: Based on Shuichi Shigeno's Initial D manga.
Your car and progress are saved on a card between visits.

Ikaruga.title: Ikaruga
Ikaruga.story: Treasure's vertical shooter, here in its 2013 NESiCAxLive arcade release. One button switches your ship between black and white: bullets of your own colour are absorbed and power up a homing attack, while the other colour destroys you. Destroying enemies in groups of three of the same colour builds chains.
special: First released in arcades in 2001 by Treasure, the makers of Radiant Silvergun.
The whole game is built around one polarity-switch button.
A classic for score chasing: chains of three same-colour kills.

LGJ.title: Let's Go Jungle! Lost on the Island of Spice
LGJ.story: A two-player gun game about a couple whose holiday goes wrong on a tropical island full of giant spiders, insects and monsters. Players hold mounted machine guns and fight back side by side, with comic scenes between the action.
special: A light-hearted, comic gun game rather than a horror one.
Made for two players sharing the experience as a couple.

LGJS.title: Let's Go Jungle! Special
LGJS.story: The big attraction version of Let's Go Jungle: two players sit inside a dome-shaped booth facing a large curved screen, with seats that move and effects that react to the action.
special: A dome theatre cabinet built for the game.

MaiMaiGreen.title: maimai GreeN
MaiMaiGreen.story: A rhythm game played on a round touch screen surrounded by eight buttons. Notes fly outward from the centre and you hit the buttons, tap and slide along the screen in time with the music. The round cabinet famously looks like a front-loading washing machine.
special: The cabinet's look earned it the nickname 'the washing machine'.
Combines physical buttons with touch-screen slides.

or2spdlx.title: OutRun 2 SP SDX
or2spdlx.story: Sega's sequel to the 1986 OutRun: drive a licensed Ferrari along sunny coastal roads, choosing left or right at each fork to plot your route to one of several goals. SP added new stages, and the SDX release brought it to newer Sega hardware.
special: The branching road from the original OutRun returns.
Licensed Ferrari cars throughout.

pacmanbr.title: Pac-Man Battle Royale
pacmanbr.story: Up to four players share one maze. Eat a power pellet and you can eat the other players as well as the ghosts; the last Pac-Man standing wins the round. The cocktail-style table cabinet puts everyone around the same screen.
special: Pac-Man turned into a party game for up to four.
Players can eat each other after a power pellet.

PokkenTournament.title: Pokken Tournament
PokkenTournament.story: A Pokemon fighting game made by Bandai Namco's Tekken team. Fights switch between a free-moving 3D Field Phase and a side-on Duel Phase, and each Pokemon fights with moves from the series. It started in Japanese arcades before coming to home consoles.
special: Built by the team behind Tekken.
Each round switches between 3D movement and classic side-on fighting.

ProjectDiva.title: Hatsune Miku: Project DIVA Arcade
ProjectDiva.story: A rhythm game starring the virtual singer Hatsune Miku and her fellow Vocaloids. Press the four face buttons as symbols reach their targets, in time with fan-made Vocaloid songs and full music videos.
special: Songs come from the Vocaloid fan community.
Every track plays with its own 3D music video.

StarWars.title: Star Wars: Battle Pod
StarWars.story: You sit inside an enclosed pod facing a curved dome screen and fly through famous Star Wars battles: the Death Star trench run, the battle of Hoth, a speeder-bike chase on Endor and the attack on the second Death Star. Fans and air blast you as you fly.
special: A wraparound dome screen fills your view.
Relives battles from the original film trilogy.

Tekken7FR.title: Tekken 7: Fated Retribution
Tekken7FR.story: The updated arcade release of Tekken 7, the chapter that set out to end the long feud of the Mishima family. Fated Retribution added new fighters and rebalanced the game ahead of its home release.
special: Tekken 7's story brings the Heihachi and Kazuya Mishima feud to a head.
Guest fighter Akuma from Street Fighter joined the roster in Tekken 7.

Theatrhythm.title: Theatrhythm Final Fantasy: All-Star Carnival
Theatrhythm.story: A rhythm game set to music from the whole Final Fantasy series. Cute chibi versions of the heroes battle and travel in time with the songs, while you hit notes on the cabinet's controls.
special: Music spans decades of Final Fantasy games.

TombRaider.title: Tomb Raider
TombRaider.story: A two-player gun game following Lara Croft through ancient tombs and jungle, with mounted guns and an enclosed, themed cabinet. It draws on the rebooted Tomb Raider games.
special: Lara Croft's first dedicated arcade gun game.

UltraStreetFighterIV.title: Ultra Street Fighter IV
UltraStreetFighterIV.story: The final version of Street Fighter IV. It added Rolento, Elena, Hugo, Poison and the new fighter Decapre, plus the Red Focus Attack, and rebalanced a cast that had grown over five years of updates.
special: The last and biggest update of Street Fighter IV.
Introduced Decapre, a new character linked to Cammy.

UnderNightInBirthExeLatest.title: Under Night In-Birth Exe:Late[st]
UnderNightInBirthExeLatest.story: A 2D fighting game from French-Bread, the studio behind Melty Blood. Fighters battle in the Hollow Night, and a tug-of-war over the GRD meter rewards whoever plays more aggressively.
special: Made by the creators of Melty Blood.
The GRD meter rewards attacking and guarding well, not just landing hits.

VT3.title: Virtua Tennis 3
VT3.story: Sega's tennis game with real professional players. Simple controls, two shot buttons and the stick to aim, hide a lot of depth in timing and placement. It came out in arcades before the home versions.
special: Licensed professional tennis players.
Easy to pick up with just two buttons.

Daytona3Single.title: Daytona Championship USA (Single Cabinet)
Daytona3Single.story: Sega's 2017 return of Daytona USA: the three classic courses remastered plus three new tracks, including the rebuilt DAYTONA International Speedway, with the famous 'Daaaytona!' song. This is the single-cabinet version: one driver against the computer cars, starting straight away with no other cabinet to wait for. On this cabinet, this is the one to pick.
special: Two Daytonas are listed: this one runs on its own; the Linked Cabinets version is set up to race other cabinets over a network.
Three remastered original courses and three new tracks.
Built for a real wheel with force feedback and a 4-speed shifter, like the 1994 original.

Daytona3Multi.title: Daytona Championship USA (Linked Cabinets)
Daytona3Multi.story: The linked version of Sega's 2017 Daytona Championship USA. In the arcade, Daytona cabinets stand side by side and are cabled together so friends race each other in the same field of cars. This copy is set up for that link: it looks for the other cabinets when it starts. With only one cabinet, the Single Cabinet version starts faster and plays the same races.
special: Two Daytonas are listed: this one is for racing other linked cabinets; the Single Cabinet version runs on its own.
Same courses and cars as the single version: three remastered originals and three new tracks.
Linked play was the heart of the original Daytona USA in 1994 too.

Crazy Taxi 3 High Roller.title: Crazy Taxi 3: High Roller
Crazy Taxi 3 High Roller.story: Pick up a fare, then get them to their stop as fast as you can, any way you can: over pavements, through parks and off jumps. The faster and wilder the ride, the bigger the tip. High Roller adds Glitter Oasis, a Las Vegas-style city, and brings back the West Coast city of the first Crazy Taxi and the Small Apple of Crazy Taxi 2. This is the 2004 PC version of the 2002 arcade and Xbox game.
special: Three cities in one game: the new Glitter Oasis plus the cities from Crazy Taxi 1 and 2.
Released in arcades on Sega's Chihiro board, the same hardware as the Xbox version.

ID4Exp.title: Initial D: Arcade Stage 4
ID4Exp.story: The first Initial D in high definition, on Sega's Lindbergh board. Based on Shuichi Shigeno's manga about street racers on the mountain passes of Gunma, Japan. You race real Japanese cars such as the Toyota AE86 down narrow downhill roads, one against one, and an IC card keeps your car, its tuning and your progress.
special: The series' move to HD widescreen.
Two linked cabinets race each other head to head.

ID5.title: Initial D: Arcade Stage 5
ID5.story: Based on Shuichi Shigeno's manga about street racers on the mountain passes of Gunma, Japan. You race real Japanese cars such as the Toyota AE86 down narrow downhill roads, one against one, and an IC card keeps your car, its tuning and your progress. Stage 5 adds courses and cars to the Lindbergh-era game.
special: Card-based progress: your car and its tuning stay with you between visits.
Two linked cabinets race each other head to head.

ID7.title: Initial D: Arcade Stage 7 AAX
ID7.story: Based on Shuichi Shigeno's manga about street racers on the mountain passes of Gunma, Japan. You race real Japanese cars such as the Toyota AE86 down narrow downhill roads, one against one, and an IC card keeps your car, its tuning and your progress. Stage 7 moved the series to Sega's RingEdge board.
special: Card-based progress and online-era features of the later arcade games.
Two linked cabinets race each other head to head.

ID8.title: Initial D: Arcade Stage 8 Infinity
ID8.story: Based on Shuichi Shigeno's manga about street racers on the mountain passes of Gunma, Japan. You race real Japanese cars such as the Toyota AE86 down narrow downhill roads, one against one, and an IC card keeps your car, its tuning and your progress.
special: The last of the original Arcade Stage numbering.
Two linked cabinets race each other head to head.

IDZ.title: Initial D: Arcade Stage Zero
IDZ.story: A fresh start for the series on new hardware with a new look. Based on Shuichi Shigeno's manga about street racers on the mountain passes of Gunma, Japan. You race real Japanese cars such as the Toyota AE86 down narrow downhill roads, one against one, and an IC card keeps your car, its tuning and your progress.
special: Rebuilt from scratch: new graphics engine and a new card system.
Two linked cabinets race each other head to head.

WMMT5.title: Wangan Midnight Maximum Tune 5
WMMT5.story: Street racing on Tokyo's Shuto Expressway at night, based on Michiharu Kusunoki's manga Wangan Midnight. Tune a real Japanese or European sports car through the story mode and race it on the expressway's long straights and tight sections; a card keeps your car and its tuning.
special: Set on the real routes of Tokyo's Shuto Expressway.
Your tuned car is saved on a card and grows stronger over many visits.

BattleGear4Tuned.title: Battle Gear 4 Tuned
BattleGear4Tuned.story: Taito's mountain-road racer with real licensed Japanese cars. Built for a full driving cabinet: wheel, pedals including a clutch, and an H-pattern gear lever, so heel-and-toe and clean gear changes win races.
special: A clutch and H-shifter game: the cabinet's left pedal and gear lever are part of the driving.
Real Japanese street cars on winding mountain courses.

GtiClub3.title: GTI Club: Supermini Festa!
GtiClub3.story: The follow-up to Konami's 1996 GTI Club: small, nimble hatchbacks race through narrow town streets, alleys and short cuts rather than closed circuits, with plenty of jumps and close calls.
special: Sequel to the 1996 arcade classic GTI Club.
Town streets full of short cuts instead of race tracks.

abc.title: After Burner Climax
abc.story: Sega's return to the 1987 jet-fighter shooter After Burner. Fly real fighter jets such as the F-14 Tomcat at full speed through canyons, over seas and cities, locking on and firing missiles at waves of enemy planes. Fill the Climax gauge to slow time and lock on to many targets at once.
special: Climax Mode slows the action down for a burst of lock-ons.
A modern sequel to the 1987 arcade classic After Burner.

Wreckfest.title: Wreckfest
Wreckfest.story: Banger racing and demolition derby from the makers of FlatOut. Cars bend, crumple and lose parts as you trade paint, so every race is as much about surviving the crashes as about the finish line.
special: Detailed crash damage: cars deform and break apart piece by piece.
Demolition derby arenas as well as races.

Burnout Paradise Remastered.title: Burnout Paradise Remastered
Burnout Paradise Remastered.story: An open city of races, stunts and crashes: drive anywhere in Paradise City, start an event at any traffic light, and take rivals out by slamming them into walls and traffic. The 2018 remaster of the 2008 original.
special: Takedowns: crashing your rivals is how you win.
The whole city is open from the start.

Project CARS.title: Project CARS
Project CARS.story: A racing simulator for wheel and pedals, with a wide range of cars from karts to prototypes, many real circuits, and weather and time of day that change during a race.
special: Built with a wheel in mind: detailed force feedback and car handling.
Changing weather and time of day during a race.

V-Rally 4.title: V-Rally 4
V-Rally 4.story: The return of the V-Rally series: rally stages against the clock on gravel, snow and tarmac, plus rallycross and other off-road events.
special: Rally stages against the clock in several countries.
Rallycross and other off-road events besides rally.

NASCAR Heat 5.title: NASCAR Heat 5
NASCAR Heat 5.story: Official NASCAR racing: the Cup Series with its drivers, cars and oval tracks, where drafting and tyre wear decide close finishes.
special: Officially licensed NASCAR cars, drivers and tracks.
Drafting in packs on the big ovals.

American Truck Simulator.title: American Truck Simulator
American Truck Simulator.story: Drive big American trucks across the western United States, delivering cargo from city to city on long highways. Not a race: careful driving, parking a trailer and keeping to the rules of the road.
special: Long-distance trucking across a scaled-down map of the American West.
Made for a wheel, pedals and a gear lever.

outrun.title: Out Run
outrun.story: Drive a red Ferrari Testarossa convertible with your passenger beside you across sunny European-style scenery, racing the clock. At the end of each stage the road forks left or right, so every run can take a different route to one of five finishes.
special: Pick your radio song before the start, including Magical Sound Shower.
Branching roads: 15 stages, five different endings.
Its sit-down cabinet moved with the steering.

vr.title: Virtua Racing
vr.story: Formula-style racing in full 3D polygons, years before most racing games: three courses of rising difficulty and four camera views you can switch while you drive.
special: One of the first arcade racers in real-time 3D polygons.
Switch between four camera views at any time.

orunners.title: OutRunners
orunners.story: The sequel to Out Run built for two: pick one of eight cars and race a friend side by side across the world, choosing left or right at each fork to set your route.
special: Head-to-head racing for two players in one cabinet.
Keeps Out Run's branching routes and music choice.

crusnusa.title: Cruis'n USA
crusnusa.story: A coast-to-coast race across America, from the Golden Gate Bridge to Washington D.C., in sports cars, a jeep and even a school bus, weaving through traffic at full speed.
special: A cross-country route through famous American places.
Arcade-style handling: big jumps, crashes and traffic.

crusnwld.title: Cruis'n World
crusnwld.story: Cruis'n goes worldwide: race through countries around the globe, with stunts in mid-air and through traffic, in the same fast, forgiving arcade style as Cruis'n USA.
special: Courses set in countries around the world.
Mid-air stunts and wheelies for show.

offroadc.title: Off Road Challenge
offroadc.story: Off-road trucks racing over desert, mud and mountain tracks with huge jumps. Earn money to upgrade your truck between races.
special: Monster jumps over rough off-road courses.
Truck upgrades bought with your winnings.

calspeed.title: California Speed
calspeed.story: Race across California, from Silicon Valley to the deserts and the coast, on courses full of jumps and short cuts, in cars ranging from sports cars to a golf cart.
special: Courses set around California.
Unusual vehicles hidden among the sports cars.

sfrushrk.title: San Francisco Rush: The Rock
sfrushrk.story: Fast, jump-filled racing through the hills of San Francisco. This edition adds the Alcatraz island course. Hidden short cuts and keys are everywhere for those who look.
special: Huge jumps down San Francisco's steep streets.
Secret short cuts and hidden keys on every course.

sf2049se.title: San Francisco Rush 2049 Special Edition
sf2049se.story: The futuristic Rush: cars with wings that open in the air, racing through a San Francisco of the year 2049, with stunt arenas and hidden routes.
special: Cars spread wings to glide through long jumps.
Stunt arenas as well as races.

F-Zero GX (USA).title: F-Zero GX
F-Zero GX (USA).story: Anti-gravity racing at extreme speed with 30 machines on twisting tubes and loops. Built by Sega's Amusement Vision for Nintendo; its arcade twin is F-Zero AX on the Triforce board.
special: 30 racers on track at once at enormous speed.
Made together by Nintendo and Sega, with an arcade version (F-Zero AX).

Mario Kart - Double Dash!! (USA).title: Mario Kart: Double Dash!!
Mario Kart - Double Dash!! (USA).story: Two characters ride each kart: one drives, the other throws the items, and you can swap them during the race. Every pair has its own special item.
special: Two riders per kart, swappable mid-race.
Each character has a special item of their own.

Auto Modellista (USA).title: Auto Modellista
Auto Modellista (USA).story: A racing game drawn like a comic book: real Japanese and European cars in a cel-shaded style, with a garage for tuning and dressing up your car.
special: Cel-shaded, comic-book graphics for real cars.
A detailed garage for tuning and dressing up cars.
